properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised by Anthony asking how CI and regression testing here could be improved, 2026-09-21.

THE OBSERVATION. This design holds 312 Verifications. Their status and `last_run_at` are written by hand, by whichever session remembered — and `last_run_at` has been in the schema since early on, with the note that it is "written by verify.rs and read by nothing in the core". Meanwhile CI runs ~48 gates on every push and throws every result away except the red/green of the job. The design's picture of what is proven and the build's knowledge of what actually ran have no connection at all.

THE COST IS ALREADY VISIBLE AND MEASURED, in three places:
· `invalidated_findings` reports `rerun_owed` as THREE-VALUED, and null means a date is missing on one side so nobody can say. Real run records collapse most of those nulls.
· The closure reading's provenance leg is 0 of 14 — every stated quantity is a number with no source. A number a gate measured on a named commit IS a source.
· 42 checks (at the last count that was taken) have never run at all, and nothing in a rollup distinguishes them from the ones marked passing.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) MINIMAL — the gate runner emits a machine-readable result file (gate name, exit code, duration, commit sha, timestamp) as a CI artifact, and nothing else changes. A later session can import it; nothing is automatic. Cheapest, and it is the option that leaves the human judgement where it is today.
(b) WRITE-BACK ON MAIN — a CI step maps gate names to Verification ids and sets status + `last_run_at` + the commit, on pushes to main only. The mapping is the hard part and would itself need a gate: an unmapped gate must be reported loudly, not skipped, which is the shape `impact_of_diff.py` already uses for unmapped files.
(c) FULL — write-back on every branch, with the run's own identity on the record.

🛑 THE OBJECTION THAT MAY KILL IT: reflow2's accepted non-goal is that a passing Verification is a claim it RECORDS and never one it VALIDATES. Write-back does not obviously cross that line — CI is a person's instrument reporting its own result, not reflow2 judging a check — but it makes reflow2 the thing that writes the claim, and whether that is still recording is Anthony's call, not mine. The second objection is smaller and concrete: an automatic writer on every branch multiplies graph writes on a store that does not branch with git, which is how phantom drift has been caused here before.
properties.name: OPEN — should a CI run write its results back into the design, so a check's status is a measurement with a date and a commit rather than something a session typed?
properties.rationale: Recorded open because option (a) is nearly free and option (c) touches an accepted non-goal, so treating them as one idea would hide the only part that needs the owner's word. The evidence that the gap is real is arithmetic already in the graph — 0 of 14 quantities sourced, and a three-valued rerun-owed whose third value exists only because run dates are missing.
